about: Term lists for scripts/check_sanitize.py — the fleet's sanitization gate for public/demo surfaces (Andrew's rule, Oct 29, 2026: public and generic, or it falls back to owner-only). This is the ONE file to maintain. Identifier values are stored as SHA-256 hashes of their normalized forms (lowercase, whitespace-collapsed; phrases hashed as their token sequence) because fleet-kit is a PUBLIC repo — the same reason family-cards-demo's CI uses generic PII shapes instead of a names list: a forbidden-names list committed in plaintext would itself publish the identifiers. To add an identifier, run: check_sanitize.py --hash-term "<term or email>" and paste the digest into the right list. Topic terms are generic category vocabulary (plus two specific service names that already appear in public CI), so they stay plaintext and readable. The allowlist is Andrew's own public identity — public on purpose — also plaintext; matching text is masked before scanning.

patterns.note: Dollar amounts with cents, comma grouping, or at least two digits. A bare single-digit $N is deliberately not matched: in shell code $1/$2 are positional parameters, not amounts (the false-positive class that tuning round 1 removed). Single-digit prices are the accepted blind spot; category language is still covered by terms.

tuning: Round 1 (Oct 29, 2026, first fleet-wide run): (1) email candidates on RFC 2606 reserved domains (example.com/.org/.net, any *.invalid) are not hits — they cannot identify anyone (aimf-protocol's spec examples, the Firebase converger's probe address); implemented in the checker. (2) The amount pattern requires cents, comma grouping, or >= 2 digits so shell positional parameters ($1, $2) stop matching.
